questions.solution:
Let $V$ be the volume, $S$ be the surface area and $r$ be the radius of the sphere.
It is given that, $\frac{d V}{d t}=1200 \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$ and $r=10 \mathrm{~cm}$

\end{aligned}$
and Surface Area of sphere,
$\begin{aligned}

& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d S}{d t}=4 \pi \cdot 2 \times 10\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right) \\
& \therefore \quad \frac{d S}{d t}=240 \mathrm{sq} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given $x^2+y^2=25\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad y=\sqrt{25-x^2} \\
& \text { Let } z=3 x+4 y \\

\end{aligned}$
Differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d z}{d x}=3+\frac{4}{2 \sqrt{25-x^2}}(-2 x)$
For maxima put $\frac{d z}{d x}=0\begin{aligned}
& 3=\frac{4 x}{\sqrt{25-x^2}} \\
& 3 \sqrt{25-x^2}=4 x \\
& 9\left(25-x^2\right)=16 x^2 \\
& 9 \times 25-9 x^2=16 x^2 \\
& 9 \times 25=(16+9) x^2 \\
& x^2=9 \\
& \therefore \quad x=3 \\
& \Rightarrow y=\sqrt{25-x^2} \Rightarrow y=4
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\quad z=3 x+4 y=3(3)+4(4)=25$
So, $\log _5[\max (3 x+4 y)]=\log _5[\max (z)]\begin{aligned}
& =\log _5[(25)]=\log _5(5)^2 \\
& =2 \log _5 5=2
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
We have, $\sum_{k=1}^6\left[\sin \frac{2 k \pi}{7}-i \cos \frac{2 \pi k}{7}\right]\begin{aligned}
& =\sum_{k=1}^6\left[(-i)\left(\cos \frac{2 k \pi}{7}+i \sin \frac{2 \pi k}{7}\right)\right] \\
& =(-i) \sum_{k=1}^6\left(\cos \frac{2 k \pi}{7}+i \sin \frac{2 \pi k}{7}\right)=(-i) \sum_{k=1}^6 \alpha^k
\end{aligned}$
Let $\alpha=\cos \frac{2 \pi k}{7}+i \sin \frac{2 \pi k}{7}=(-i)\left(\alpha+\alpha^2+\alpha^3+\ldots+\alpha^5\right)$
Here, $\alpha+\alpha^2+\alpha^3+\ldots+\alpha^6$ follows G.P. so its sum.
$\mathrm{S}=\frac{\alpha\left(1-\alpha^6\right)}{1-\alpha}=\frac{\alpha-\alpha^7}{1-\alpha}=\frac{\alpha-1}{1-\alpha}=i$
\left[\because \alpha^7=\cos 2 \pi+i \sin 2 \pi=1\right]

Thus, $\alpha=-i(-1)\alpha=i$

questions.q: If $\sin A+\sin B+\sin C=0$ and $\cos A+\cos B+\cos C=0$, then $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Here, we have the pattern of data in $\cos x$ and $\sin x$, so let's use the method of polar form of complex number.
Polar form of complex number,
$z=\cos \theta+i \sin \theta$
then $\bar{z}=\cos \theta-i \sin \theta$
and $z \bar{z}=1\Rightarrow \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}$
Let $z_1=\cos A+i \sin Az_2=\cos B+i \sin B$
and $z_3=\cos C+i \sin C$
Then, $\quad \bar{z}_1=\cos A-i \sin A\begin{gathered}
\bar{z}_2=\cos B-i \sin B \\
z_3=\cos C-\sin C
\end{gathered}$
Now, to find $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)\begin{aligned}
& \bar{z}_1+\bar{z}_2+\bar{z}_3=(\cos A-i \sin A) \\
& +(\cos B-i \sin B)+(\cos C-i \sin C) \\
& =(\cos A+\cos B+\cos C)-i(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)=0 \\
& \frac{1}{z_1}+\frac{1}{z_2}+\frac{1}{z_3}=0 \quad\left[\because \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}\right] \\
& z_1 z_2+z_2 z_3+z_3 z_1=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A+i \sin A)(\cos B+i \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A \cos B-\sin A \sin B) \\
& +i(\sin A \cos B+\cos A \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)+i \sin (A+B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing the real part, we get
$\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)=0$

questions.q: The pressure on a circular plate is measured by measuring the force on the plate and the radius of the plate. If the errors in measurement of the force and the radius are $5 \%$ and $3 \%$ respectively, the percentage of error in the measurement of pressure is
questions.solution:
We have
$\begin{aligned}
& p=\frac{F}{A}=\frac{F}{\pi R^2} \\
& \text { So, } \frac{\Delta p}{p} \times 100=\frac{\Delta F}{F} \times 100+2 \frac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100 \\
& =5+2(3)=5+6=11 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta p}{p} \times 100=11 \%
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The amplitude of a simple pendulum is $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. When the pendulum is at a displacement of $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mean position, the ratio of kinetic and potential energies at that point is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  \mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2\left(A^2-x^2\right) \\
& \mathrm{P} . \mathrm{E}=\frac{1}{2} k x^2=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2
\end{aligned}$
Therefore, the ratio
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{KE}}{\mathrm{PE}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2\left(A^2-x^2\right)}{\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 x^2} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}}{\mathrm{PE}}=\frac{\mathrm{A}^2-\mathrm{x}^2}{\mathrm{x}^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{10^2-4^2}{4^2}=\frac{84}{16} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{KE}}{\mathrm{PE}}=\frac{21}{4}=5.25
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

As, the temperature falls so internal energy will decrease by $4.5 \mathrm{~J}$
